item.title: Quasiconformal characterization of Schottky sets
item.headline: When rounding holes two at a time guarantees a global reshaping
item.summary: A theorem characterizes when a perforated spherical surface can be reshaped to have circular holes with bounded distortion. Its uniform pairwise condition is essential.

evidence.question: When do pairwise geometric constraints control an entire shape?
evidence.method: Mathematical proof using circle reflections, curve-family estimates, and limits of finite approximations.
evidence.limitations: A conditional existence theorem, not a numerical algorithm.

explainer.finding: For disjoint regions bounded by simple closed curves, roundability of every pair with one common distortion bound guarantees a global rounding.
explainer.method: The proof controls finite configurations, then passes to a limit while preserving distortion bounds.
explainer.meaning: Imagine a surface with infinitely many holes. Pairwise compatibility can guarantee one coherent reshaping; separately rounding each hole would not suffice.
explainer.limits: Quasiconformal means locally bounded stretching imbalance, not preserved lengths. Distinct boundaries and the uniform pairwise hypothesis matter. A purely topological characterization remains open.
